correctness.rationale: A nonresolving set lies in an equal-distance bisector E(X,Y). Every pair of 2-subsets X,Y intersects once or not at all, producing respectively A_B=all pairs outside B plus B, or D_{P|Q}=four crossing pairs plus pairs outside P∪Q. Their sizes differ by 2(n-5). Inclusion comparison of root-graph components leaves D swallowed by A only at n=6 (A swallowed by D at n=4); hence all maximal families and exact counts follow. KG(n,2) at n>=5 has diameter two and complement adjacency, so each equal-distance relation for distinct landmark vertices coincides, including zeros treated separately. Independent BFS enumerated every pair bisector and maximal containment for n=4..9 and confirmed formulas for KG at n>=5.

originality.rationale: Korivand–Khashyarmanesh–Tavakoli introduce metric dimension threshold and prove Petersen KG(5,2) threshold 5. Bailey et al treat minimum resolving dimension of Johnson/Kneser graphs, a different quantifier. Kratica et al study equidistant dimension with opposite existential condition. These do not provide the all-n complete maximal-nonresolving-bisector classification.

value.rationale: A natural worst-case landmark-identifiability invariant is determined for all triangular graphs and two-set Kneser complements. Exact finite obstruction classification, counts, and sharp threshold are useful beyond ordinary metric dimension, and the equality of resolving families under graph complement is structural.

final_claim: For triangular graph T_n=J(n,2), n>=4, universal resolving threshold is 5 at n=4,5 and binom(n-2,2)+2 for n>=6, with all inclusion-maximal nonresolving landmark sets exactly bisectors of Type A (K_{n-2} disjoint K_2) and Type D (C4 disjoint K_{n-4}) under stated n exceptions; same resolving and nonresolving subsets for KG(n,2) at n>=5.
limitations: Bounded independent experiments corroborate but do not replace the unrestricted analytic proof (or complete finite exhaustive argument for Pappus).
